---
title: How an agent reaches Frame Job
description: What an AI agent can do in Frame Job over MCP, how it connects, what happens when Frame Job is closed, and who is allowed in.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Frame Job serves its whole editor as MCP tools, so an AI agent such as Claude Code can open projects, cut, style, check its work frame by frame and export, as you do in the window.

<AtAGlance
  where="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ MCP"
  needs="An MCP client, such as Claude Code. No key and no account on Frame Job's side."
/>

## The whole editor as tools

A shipped Frame Job publishes 125 tools. Every edit you can make in the window has one, and the rest cover what sits around an edit: opening and saving projects, moving the playhead, reading the project, rendering a frame, exporting. [All tools](/mcp/tools/) lists them.

An agent's edit goes through the same place your own clicks go. It shows in the window at once, marks the project as edited, and is one undo step you can take back with <kbd>⌘Z</kbd>.

A tool checks what it's given before it does anything. An argument it doesn't take is refused by name, with the list of what it does take, so a model can read the answer and correct itself. [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/) has the rest.

To connect a client, see [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/).

## The framejob-mcp helper

Most MCP clients start a small server of their own and talk to it over standard input and output. For them, the app carries one:

```
Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp
```

It's called `framejob-mcp`, and it's the way a client such as Claude Code connects. There's no runtime to install. The client starts the helper, and the helper reaches Frame Job over a [local socket](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#the-local-agent-socket).

The helper does three things beyond passing messages along: it answers a client that's starting up, it [lists the tools when Frame Job can't](#the-tool-list-with-frame-job-closed), and it [opens Frame Job on the first tool call](#opening-on-the-first-tool-call).

Register it at its path inside the app, because it works only from there. See [The helper stays in the bundle](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#the-helper-stays-in-the-bundle).

## The tool list with Frame Job closed

Starting an MCP client never opens the video editor. The helper answers the client's first messages itself, so a session starts with nothing on screen, and asking for the tool list never launches Frame Job either.

When a client asks for the tool list, the helper asks the running app first. It answers from a copy of the list stored in the app when:

- Frame Job isn't running.
- Frame Job doesn't answer within 5 seconds, for example because another client's long call is holding it.

So a client always sees every tool, and if the stored list turns out to differ from the running app's, [the helper says so](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#tool-list-changes).

## Opening on the first tool call

If a tool call finds Frame Job not running, the helper launches its own copy of the app in the background and waits for it. The app doesn't come to the front. Once it's listening, the call runs as usual.

- The helper waits up to 60 seconds. See [The launch wait](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#the-launch-wait), and [Failed launches](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#failed-launches) for what happens when that runs out.
- Several clients calling at once start only one copy.
- This also happens if you quit Frame Job in the middle of a session: the next tool call opens it again.

Only programs running under your own account can connect, and any of them can while Frame Job is running. There's no password or per-client approval, and no network port, so nothing on another machine can reach it.

## Assistant rules do not bind an MCP client

The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) inside Frame Job works under rules of its own. It can't call some tools, and it asks you before it calls others. | Tool | The Assistant | An MCP client |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine | Can't call it | Calls it directly |
| `export`, `export_captions`, `save_project`, `consolidate_media`, `export_graphic` | Asks you first | Calls it directly |
| `new_project_from_range`, `make_vertical_version` when the call names a path | Asks you first | Calls it directly |

## Settings has no tool

No MCP tool reads or writes anything in [Settings](/reference/settings/). An agent can't set or read a key, the Assistant's model, the AssemblyAI region or Background render. Only a person sets those, in **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>).

An agent's cloud tools do use what's saved there. `transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine and `transcribe_for_fillers` send with your key and region, so you have to set the key first. Without one they answer "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription."

## Good to know

- Calls run one at a time, across every connected client and the Assistant, so a long call holds the next one until it ends.
- A tool call never asks you anything. Anything that needs a question answered or a system permission granted has to be done by a person first. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/).

## Related

- [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/)
- [The helper and the socket](/mcp/helper-and-socket/)
- [A typical session](/mcp/typical-session/)
- [All tools](/mcp/tools/)

---
title: Connect a client
description: Add Frame Job to Claude Code with one copied command, or point Claude Desktop or any other stdio MCP client at the bundled helper.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

An MCP client connects to Frame Job through `framejob-mcp`, a helper inside the app. You register the helper once, and Frame Job's tools are there whenever the client runs.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings…"
  keys="⌘,"
  where="The MCP section, at the top of Settings"
  needs="An MCP client that starts a stdio server, such as Claude Code or Claude Desktop."
/>

## Connect Claude Code

<Steps>

1. Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>). The **MCP** section is at the top.

2. Choose **Copy MCP Command**. The section reads "Copied. Paste it into Terminal and press Return."

3. Paste the command into Terminal and press <kbd>Return</kbd>.

</Steps>

For a copy of Frame Job in `/Applications`, the command is:

```sh
claude mcp add --scope user framejob -- '/Applications/Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp'
```

`--scope user` makes Frame Job's tools available in every Claude Code project.

Frame Job doesn't have to be open. Claude Code can start and list the tools with the app closed, and the first tool call [opens it in the background](/mcp/overview/#opening-on-the-first-tool-call).

## Claude Desktop and other stdio clients

Any MCP client that starts a stdio server can use the same helper, by its path. Copy MCP Command writes the Claude Code command only, so for anything else you enter the path by hand.

For Claude Desktop, add it to `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "framejob": {
      "command": "/Applications/Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

If your copy of Frame Job lives somewhere else, use [the path Settings shows](#the-helper-path-in-settings). A client that can speak HTTP over a Unix socket can skip the helper and [connect directly](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#streamable-http-over-the-socket).

## The MCP section in Settings

**MCP** is the first of the sections in Settings. From top to bottom it holds two short paragraphs on how a client reaches Frame Job, the helper's path, **Copy MCP Command** and a status line.

### The helper path in Settings

The section shows the full path of `framejob-mcp` inside the copy of Frame Job you're running, ending `Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp`. You can select it and copy it.

### Copy MCP Command

**Copy MCP Command** puts the Claude Code command for this copy of Frame Job on the clipboard, with the path filled in and quoted for the shell. It always names the helper inside the copy you opened Settings from, so a copy in `~/Applications` or a build folder registers itself.

The path doesn't follow the app. If you move Frame Job, copy the command again and register the new path.

The button isn't an edit, so no agent tool does the same thing.

### The missing helper warning

If the helper is missing from this copy of Frame Job, or can't be run, **Copy MCP Command** is dimmed and the status line reads "framejob-mcp is missing from this copy of Frame Job."

Frame Job checks each time Settings opens. If the helper disappears while the window is open, pressing the button copies nothing and shows the same line.

## Testing a second copy

This is for testing, not everyday use. Setting the environment variable `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` to a path moves the socket there, so a test copy of Frame Job stays apart from your everyday one. Set it for both Frame Job and `framejob-mcp`.

Setting it for the helper alone is often enough. When a tool call finds nothing at that path, the helper launches the copy it belongs to and passes the path on. See [A custom socket path](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#a-custom-socket-path) for the rules.

## Related

- [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/)
- [The helper and the socket](/mcp/helper-and-socket/)
- [A typical session](/mcp/typical-session/)
- [Settings](/reference/settings/)

---
title: The helper and the socket
description: How framejob-mcp reaches Frame Job, what it launches and how long it waits, the local socket and its permissions, and what each error means.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

This page is the detail behind the connection: what the helper will and won't launch, how the socket is guarded, and what to read when a client can't get through. To set up a client, see [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/).

<AtAGlance
  where={['Helper: Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp', 'Socket: ~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock']}
/>

## The helper stays in the bundle

The helper launches only the Frame Job it belongs to, so each copy of the app opens itself and never another copy. Always register it at its path inside the app.

A helper moved out of the app can neither read the stored tool list nor launch Frame Job. A client can still start a session with it, but asking for the tool list answers an error when no Frame Job is running, and a tool call that finds no Frame Job answers a sentence naming the executable:

```
framejob-mcp is not inside a Frame Job bundle: <path> is not <X>.app/Contents/Helpers/<name>, so there is no Frame Job to launch
```

The helper doesn't check which copy answers on the socket. If you have two copies of Frame Job and one is already running, the other's helper talks to the running one.

## The local agent socket

Frame Job opens a local Unix socket every time it launches, at:

```
~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock
```

There's no switch to turn it on or off, and no network port. See [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/) for the folders around it.

### The socket's folder and permissions

The socket sits in the `Agent` folder, and those permissions are its only protection. The folder is `0700` and the socket is `0600`, so only programs running as you can open it. Frame Job makes the folder that way when it's missing.

The folder has to be a real folder, not a symlink. It has to be owned by you, with no permissions for group or others. If it isn't, Frame Job reports the problem in the [log](#socket-status-in-the-log) and doesn't open the socket. It never loosens or repairs the folder itself, so a wrong mode is yours to fix.

### Streamable HTTP over the socket

The socket serves MCP as streamable HTTP, so a client that can speak HTTP over a Unix socket can connect directly, without the helper.

- Each request is one JSON-RPC `POST /mcp`, answered with a single JSON response. There's no event stream and no session id.
- Any method but `POST` answers HTTP 405.
- A request body over 8 MiB answers HTTP 413.
- A message that isn't JSON answers HTTP 400 with error `-32700`.
- A notification answers HTTP 202 with no body.
- A batch is answered element by element. The helper, by contrast, doesn't take batches.

A direct client gets none of the helper's help. It has no stored tool list, and nothing launches Frame Job for it.

### One copy holds the socket

With several copies of Frame Job open, the first owns the socket. A later copy finds that something answers there, leaves it alone and opens none. The later copy works normally in its window, but no agent can reach it.

If the file at the path isn't a socket at all, Frame Job leaves that alone too, and opens nothing.

### Stale socket cleanup

A socket file left behind by a copy that crashed is removed and replaced automatically. Only a socket that answers counts as another copy, so a leftover never stops the next launch.

### The socket released at quit

Quitting removes the socket file if it's still this copy's. A tool call in flight can't hold up the quit.

### Socket status in the log

A launch that can't open the socket logs why and carries on, with no dialog. Frame Job works as usual, and no agent can reach that copy. Look in the Console app for a line starting "Frame Job agent socket".

| The log says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `Frame Job agent socket listening at <path>` | The socket is open. |
| `… not bound: another instance answers at <path>; this one binds none` | [Another copy](#one-copy-holds-the-socket) holds the socket. |
| `… not bound: <folder> is mode 0755; the socket's folder must be its owner's alone (0700)` | The folder lets someone else in. The mode shown is the one it has. |
| `… not bound: <folder> is not a folder (a symlink is refused)` | The folder is a symlink or a file. |
| `… not bound: <folder> is owned by uid 501, not this user (502)` | Someone else owns the folder. |
| `… not bound: <path> exists and is not a socket; it is left alone` | Something else is at the socket's path. Frame Job won't delete it. |
| `… not bound: socket path is 110 bytes; macOS allows 103: <path>` | A [custom path](#a-custom-socket-path) is too long. |
| `… not bound: socket path must be absolute: <path>` | A custom path doesn't start at the root. |

### A custom socket path

The environment variable `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` moves the socket, for both the app and the helper. It's for [testing a second copy](/mcp/connect-a-client/#testing-a-second-copy).

- The path must be absolute, and at most 103 bytes. That's a macOS limit.
- An empty value means the default path.
- The path's folder follows the same [rules](#the-sockets-folder-and-permissions) as the default one. A folder that already exists with mode `0755` won't do. A missing folder is made with the right mode.
- Only the socket moves. The test copy still shares your everyday copy's preferences.

When the helper launches Frame Job for a custom socket, it passes the path on, tells macOS not to restore the app's windows from last time, and writes the app's error output to `framejob-launch.log` beside the socket. A launch for your own socket does none of this, so your Frame Job opens as yours.

## When the helper launches Frame Job

The helper launches Frame Job when a [tool call finds nothing listening](/mcp/overview/#opening-on-the-first-tool-call). It runs `open -n -g` on its own app, so the app stays in the background. Nothing else launches it: not a client starting up, not `ping`, not a request for the tool list.

### One launch between several clients

Two clients that both find no Frame Job launch one copy between them, not two. A lock file, `agent.launch.lock`, sits beside the socket, and the helper holds it until the launched copy answers or the wait ends. Another helper waiting on that lock looks again once it gets it, and finds the copy already running.

Calls made at the same moment in one client session also launch at most once.

### The launch wait

The helper waits up to 60 seconds for a launched Frame Job to start listening. To change that, set the environment variable `RC_MCP_LAUNCH_WAIT` for the helper to a positive whole number of seconds. Any other value means 60.

### Failed launches

If a launched Frame Job never starts listening, the call answers:

```
Frame Job did not answer at <socket> within 60 s of launching <bundle>
```

That client session then stops launching. While nothing answers on the socket, its later calls answer the same sentence with this added, and start no more copies:

```
that instance may still be running, so this session will not launch another — quit it and check <folder>
```

The usual cause is the socket's folder. A copy that can't open the socket keeps running in the background and [logs why](#socket-status-in-the-log). To recover:

1. Quit the stray copy of Frame Job.
2. Check the folder the sentence names, and the log.
3. Open Frame Job yourself, or start a new client session. The session that failed won't launch again, but it does use a Frame Job that answers.

## While a client is connected

### Long calls are never timed out

A forwarded tool call can take as long as it needs, so a long recording or analysis is never cut off by the helper. Only the helper's own request for the tool list has a limit, the [5 seconds](/mcp/overview/#the-tool-list-with-frame-job-closed) before it falls back to the stored list.

A `ping` is answered even while a long call holds the app, because the helper answers it itself.

If the client closes, the helper exits at once, without waiting for a call in flight.

### Errors from the helper

A call the helper couldn't deliver comes back as an ordinary tool result with `isError: true` and a plain sentence, so a model can read it.

| The call answers | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `could not connect to Frame Job at <path>: <reason>` | The socket is there but can't be reached, for example because of its permissions. |
| `/usr/bin/open <bundle> failed (<status>): <reason>` | macOS couldn't launch the app. |
| `Frame Job did not answer at <socket> within …` | See [Failed launches](#failed-launches). |
| `could not read Frame Job's answer at <path>: the answer is over 8 MiB` | The helper won't read an answer larger than 8 MiB. |
| `HOME is not set, so the agent socket's path is unknown` | The helper started with no home folder in its environment, and no custom path. |

Other failures are JSON-RPC errors:

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `-32700` | The line isn't JSON. The answer has a null id. |
| `-32600` | The message is a batch, or isn't a JSON object. A batch and a non-object answer with a null id. A method that isn't a string answers this too, with the request's id. |
| `-32601` | Frame Job isn't answering and the method is one the helper can't handle itself, or Frame Job doesn't know the method. |
| `-32603` | The tool list couldn't be answered from the app or from the stored copy, `Contents/Resources/agent-catalog.json`. The message names both reasons. |

The helper passes any method but `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list` and `tools/call` to the app when it answers. Notifications and responses from a client are dropped and never forwarded.

The helper's standard output carries protocol only. Everything else it says goes to standard error, each line starting `framejob-mcp: `, so that's where to look in a client's logs.

### Protocol versions

Frame Job speaks three MCP protocol revisions: `2024-11-05`, `2025-03-26` and `2025-06-18`. It answers with the revision a client asks for, or `2025-06-18` if it asks for any other. The app and the helper work from the same list.

The helper's `initialize` answer names the server `framejob`, gives the version of the Frame Job it belongs to, and declares tools with `listChanged`.

### Tool list changes

A list from the stored copy can differ from the running app's, for example when another copy of Frame Job holds the socket. ---
title: The helper and the socket
description: How framejob-mcp reaches Frame Job, what it launches and how long it waits, the local socket and its permissions, and what each error means.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

This page is the detail behind the connection: what the helper will and won't launch, how the socket is guarded, and what to read when a client can't get through. To set up a client, see [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/).

<AtAGlance
  where={['Helper: Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp', 'Socket: ~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock']}
/>

## The helper stays in the bundle

The helper launches only the Frame Job it belongs to, so each copy of the app opens itself and never another copy. Always register it at its path inside the app.

A helper moved out of the app can neither read the stored tool list nor launch Frame Job. A client can still start a session with it, but asking for the tool list answers an error when no Frame Job is running, and a tool call that finds no Frame Job answers a sentence naming the executable:

```
framejob-mcp is not inside a Frame Job bundle: <path> is not <X>.app/Contents/Helpers/<name>, so there is no Frame Job to launch
```

The helper doesn't check which copy answers on the socket. If you have two copies of Frame Job and one is already running, the other's helper talks to the running one.

## The local agent socket

Frame Job opens a local Unix socket every time it launches, at:

```
~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock
```

There's no switch to turn it on or off, and no network port. See [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/) for the folders around it.

### The socket's folder and permissions

The socket sits in the `Agent` folder, and those permissions are its only protection. The folder is `0700` and the socket is `0600`, so only programs running as you can open it. Frame Job makes the folder that way when it's missing.

The folder has to be a real folder, not a symlink. It has to be owned by you, with no permissions for group or others. If it isn't, Frame Job reports the problem in the [log](#socket-status-in-the-log) and doesn't open the socket. It never loosens or repairs the folder itself, so a wrong mode is yours to fix.

### Streamable HTTP over the socket

The socket serves MCP as streamable HTTP, so a client that can speak HTTP over a Unix socket can connect directly, without the helper.

- Each request is one JSON-RPC `POST /mcp`, answered with a single JSON response. There's no event stream and no session id.
- Any method but `POST` answers HTTP 405.
- A request body over 8 MiB answers HTTP 413.
- A message that isn't JSON answers HTTP 400 with error `-32700`.
- A notification answers HTTP 202 with no body.
- A batch is answered element by element. The helper, by contrast, doesn't take batches.

A direct client gets none of the helper's help. It has no stored tool list, and nothing launches Frame Job for it.

### One copy holds the socket

With several copies of Frame Job open, the first owns the socket. A later copy finds that something answers there, leaves it alone and opens none. The later copy works normally in its window, but no agent can reach it.

If the file at the path isn't a socket at all, Frame Job leaves that alone too, and opens nothing.

### Stale socket cleanup

A socket file left behind by a copy that crashed is removed and replaced automatically. Only a socket that answers counts as another copy, so a leftover never stops the next launch.

### The socket released at quit

Quitting removes the socket file if it's still this copy's. A tool call in flight can't hold up the quit.

### Socket status in the log

A launch that can't open the socket logs why and carries on, with no dialog. Frame Job works as usual, and no agent can reach that copy. Look in the Console app for a line starting "Frame Job agent socket".

| The log says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `Frame Job agent socket listening at <path>` | The socket is open. |
| `… not bound: another instance answers at <path>; this one binds none` | [Another copy](#one-copy-holds-the-socket) holds the socket. |
| `… not bound: <folder> is mode 0755; the socket's folder must be its owner's alone (0700)` | The folder lets someone else in. The mode shown is the one it has. |
| `… not bound: <folder> is not a folder (a symlink is refused)` | The folder is a symlink or a file. |
| `… not bound: <folder> is owned by uid 501, not this user (502)` | Someone else owns the folder. |
| `… not bound: <path> exists and is not a socket; it is left alone` | Something else is at the socket's path. Frame Job won't delete it. |
| `… not bound: socket path is 110 bytes; macOS allows 103: <path>` | A [custom path](#a-custom-socket-path) is too long. |
| `… not bound: socket path must be absolute: <path>` | A custom path doesn't start at the root. |

### A custom socket path

The environment variable `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` moves the socket, for both the app and the helper. It's for [testing a second copy](/mcp/connect-a-client/#testing-a-second-copy).

- The path must be absolute, and at most 103 bytes. That's a macOS limit.
- An empty value means the default path.
- The path's folder follows the same [rules](#the-sockets-folder-and-permissions) as the default one. A folder that already exists with mode `0755` won't do. A missing folder is made with the right mode.
- Only the socket moves. The test copy still shares your everyday copy's preferences.

When the helper launches Frame Job for a custom socket, it passes the path on, tells macOS not to restore the app's windows from last time, and writes the app's error output to `framejob-launch.log` beside the socket. A launch for your own socket does none of this, so your Frame Job opens as yours.

## When the helper launches Frame Job

The helper launches Frame Job when a [tool call finds nothing listening](/mcp/overview/#opening-on-the-first-tool-call). It runs `open -n -g` on its own app, so the app stays in the background. Nothing else launches it: not a client starting up, not `ping`, not a request for the tool list.

### One launch between several clients

Two clients that both find no Frame Job launch one copy between them, not two. A lock file, `agent.launch.lock`, sits beside the socket, and the helper holds it until the launched copy answers or the wait ends. Another helper waiting on that lock looks again once it gets it, and finds the copy already running.

Calls made at the same moment in one client session also launch at most once.

### The launch wait

The helper waits up to 60 seconds for a launched Frame Job to start listening. To change that, set the environment variable `RC_MCP_LAUNCH_WAIT` for the helper to a positive whole number of seconds. Any other value means 60.

### Failed launches

If a launched Frame Job never starts listening, the call answers:

```
Frame Job did not answer at <socket> within 60 s of launching <bundle>
```

That client session then stops launching. While nothing answers on the socket, its later calls answer the same sentence with this added, and start no more copies:

```
that instance may still be running, so this session will not launch another — quit it and check <folder>
```

The usual cause is the socket's folder. A copy that can't open the socket keeps running in the background and [logs why](#socket-status-in-the-log). To recover:

1. Quit the stray copy of Frame Job.
2. Check the folder the sentence names, and the log.
3. Open Frame Job yourself, or start a new client session. The session that failed won't launch again, but it does use a Frame Job that answers.

## While a client is connected

### Long calls are never timed out

A forwarded tool call can take as long as it needs, so a long recording or analysis is never cut off by the helper. Only the helper's own request for the tool list has a limit, the [5 seconds](/mcp/overview/#the-tool-list-with-frame-job-closed) before it falls back to the stored list.

A `ping` is answered even while a long call holds the app, because the helper answers it itself.

If the client closes, the helper exits at once, without waiting for a call in flight.

### Errors from the helper

A call the helper couldn't deliver comes back as an ordinary tool result with `isError: true` and a plain sentence, so a model can read it.

| The call answers | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `could not connect to Frame Job at <path>: <reason>` | The socket is there but can't be reached, for example because of its permissions. |
| `/usr/bin/open <bundle> failed (<status>): <reason>` | macOS couldn't launch the app. |
| `Frame Job did not answer at <socket> within …` | See [Failed launches](#failed-launches). |
| `could not read Frame Job's answer at <path>: the answer is over 8 MiB` | The helper won't read an answer larger than 8 MiB. |
| `HOME is not set, so the agent socket's path is unknown` | The helper started with no home folder in its environment, and no custom path. |

Other failures are JSON-RPC errors:

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `-32700` | The line isn't JSON. The answer has a null id. |
| `-32600` | The message is a batch, or isn't a JSON object. A batch and a non-object answer with a null id. A method that isn't a string answers this too, with the request's id. |
| `-32601` | Frame Job isn't answering and the method is one the helper can't handle itself, or Frame Job doesn't know the method. |
| `-32603` | The tool list couldn't be answered from the app or from the stored copy, `Contents/Resources/agent-catalog.json`. The message names both reasons. |

The helper's standard output carries protocol only. Everything else it says goes to standard error, each line starting `framejob-mcp: `, so that's where to look in a client's logs.

### Protocol versions

Frame Job speaks three MCP protocol revisions: `2024-11-05`, `2025-03-26` and `2025-06-18`. It answers with the revision a client asks for, or `2025-06-18` if it asks for any other. The app and the helper work from the same list.

The helper's `initialize` answer names the server `framejob`, gives the version of the Frame Job it belongs to, and declares tools with `listChanged`.

### Tool list changes

A list from the stored copy can differ from the running app's, for example when another copy of Frame Job holds the socket. So after a client gets the stored list, or after a launch, the helper asks the app for its list following the next forwarded call. If it differs from what the client was last given, the helper sends `notifications/tools/list_changed` and the client can read it again.

The lists are compared by their content, so a difference in key order doesn't count.

## Related

- [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/)
- [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/)
- [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/)
- [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/)

---
title: How an agent reaches Frame Job
description: What an AI agent can do in Frame Job over MCP, how it connects, what happens when Frame Job is closed, and who is allowed in.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Frame Job serves its whole editor as MCP tools, so an AI agent such as Claude Code can open projects, cut, style, check its work frame by frame and export, as you do in the window.

<AtAGlance
  where="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ MCP"
  needs="An MCP client, such as Claude Code. No key and no account on Frame Job's side."
/>

## The whole editor as tools

A shipped Frame Job publishes 125 tools. Every edit you can make in the window has one, and the rest cover what sits around an edit: opening and saving projects, moving the playhead, reading the project, rendering a frame, exporting. [All tools](/mcp/tools/) lists them.

An agent's edit goes through the same place your own clicks go. It shows in the window at once, marks the project as edited, and is one undo step you can take back with <kbd>⌘Z</kbd>.

A tool checks what it's given before it does anything. An argument it doesn't take is refused by name, with the list of what it does take, so a model can read the answer and correct itself. [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/) has the rest.

To connect a client, see [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/).

## The framejob-mcp helper

Most MCP clients start a small server of their own and talk to it over standard input and output. For them, the app carries one:

```
Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp
```

It's called `framejob-mcp`, and it's the way a client such as Claude Code connects. There's no runtime to install. The client starts the helper, and the helper reaches Frame Job over a [local socket](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#the-local-agent-socket).

The helper does three things beyond passing messages along: it answers a client that's starting up, it [lists the tools when Frame Job can't](#the-tool-list-with-frame-job-closed), and it [opens Frame Job on the first tool call](#opening-on-the-first-tool-call).

Register it at its path inside the app, because it works only from there. See [The helper stays in the bundle](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#the-helper-stays-in-the-bundle).

## The tool list with Frame Job closed

Starting an MCP client never opens the video editor. The helper answers the client's first messages itself, so a session starts with nothing on screen, and asking for the tool list never launches Frame Job either.

When a client asks for the tool list, the helper asks the running app first. It answers from a copy of the list stored in the app when:

- Frame Job isn't running.
- Frame Job doesn't answer within 5 seconds, for example because another client's long call is holding it.

So a client always sees every tool, and if the stored list turns out to differ from the running app's, [the helper says so](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#tool-list-changes).

## Opening on the first tool call

If a tool call finds Frame Job not running, the helper launches its own copy of the app in the background and waits for it. The app doesn't come to the front. Once it's listening, the call runs as usual.

- The helper waits up to 60 seconds. See [The launch wait](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#the-launch-wait), and [Failed launches](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#failed-launches) for what happens when that runs out.
- Several clients calling at once start only one copy.
- This also happens if you quit Frame Job in the middle of a session: the next tool call opens it again.

## Who can connect

Only programs running under your own account can connect, and any of them can while Frame Job is running. There's no password or per-client approval, and no network port, so nothing on another machine can reach it.

The socket's permissions are the whole of this protection, so Frame Job is strict about them. If they're wrong it doesn't open the socket at all. See [The socket's folder and permissions](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#the-sockets-folder-and-permissions).

## Assistant rules do not bind an MCP client

The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) inside Frame Job works under rules of its own. It can't call some tools, and it asks you before it calls others. Those rules belong to the Assistant, not to the tools. A client connected over MCP calls every tool directly, and nothing asks you first.

| Tool | The Assistant | An MCP client |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `record_screen`, `close_project`, `transcribe_for_fillers` | Can't call it | Calls it directly |
| `transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine | Can't call it | Calls it directly |
| `export`, `export_captions`, `save_project`, `consolidate_media`, `export_graphic` | Asks you first | Calls it directly |
| `new_project_from_range`, `make_vertical_version` when the call names a path | Asks you first | Calls it directly |

So a connected agent can spend your AssemblyAI credit, or replace a file with an export, without a question from Frame Job. If you want a check on that, use the permission settings in your MCP client.

## Settings has no tool

No MCP tool reads or writes anything in [Settings](/reference/settings/). An agent can't set or read a key, the Assistant's model, the AssemblyAI region or Background render. Only a person sets those, in **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>).

An agent's cloud tools do use what's saved there. `transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine and `transcribe_for_fillers` send with your key and region, so you have to set the key first. Without one they answer "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription."

## Good to know

- Calls run one at a time, across every connected client and the Assistant, so a long call holds the next one until it ends.
- A tool call never asks you anything. Anything that needs a question answered or a system permission granted has to be done by a person first. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/).

## Related

- [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/)
- [The helper and the socket](/mcp/helper-and-socket/)
- [A typical session](/mcp/typical-session/)
- [All tools](/mcp/tools/)

title: Connect a client
description: Add Frame Job to Claude Code with one copied command, or point Claude Desktop or any other stdio MCP client at the bundled helper.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

An MCP client connects to Frame Job through `framejob-mcp`, a helper inside the app. You register the helper once, and Frame Job's tools are there whenever the client runs.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings…"
  keys="⌘,"
  where="The MCP section, at the top of Settings"
  needs="An MCP client that starts a stdio server, such as Claude Code or Claude Desktop."
/>

## Connect Claude Code

<Steps>

1. Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>). The **MCP** section is at the top.

2. Choose **Copy MCP Command**. The section reads "Copied. Paste it into Terminal and press Return."

3. Paste the command into Terminal and press <kbd>Return</kbd>.

</Steps>

For a copy of Frame Job in `/Applications`, the command is:

```sh
claude mcp add --scope user framejob -- '/Applications/Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp'
```

`--scope user` makes Frame Job's tools available in every Claude Code project.

Frame Job doesn't have to be open. Claude Code can start and list the tools with the app closed, and the first tool call [opens it in the background](/mcp/overview/#opening-on-the-first-tool-call).

## Claude Desktop and other stdio clients

Any MCP client that starts a stdio server can use the same helper, by its path. Copy MCP Command writes the Claude Code command only, so for anything else you enter the path by hand.

For Claude Desktop, add it to `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "framejob": {
      "command": "/Applications/Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

If your copy of Frame Job lives somewhere else, use [the path Settings shows](#the-helper-path-in-settings). A client that can speak HTTP over a Unix socket can skip the helper and [connect directly](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#streamable-http-over-the-socket).

## The MCP section in Settings

**MCP** is the first of the sections in Settings. From top to bottom it holds two short paragraphs on how a client reaches Frame Job, the helper's path, **Copy MCP Command** and a status line.

### The helper path in Settings

The section shows the full path of `framejob-mcp` inside the copy of Frame Job you're running, ending `Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp`. You can select it and copy it.

### Copy MCP Command

**Copy MCP Command** puts the Claude Code command for this copy of Frame Job on the clipboard, with the path filled in and quoted for the shell. It always names the helper inside the copy you opened Settings from, so a copy in `~/Applications` or a build folder registers itself.

The path doesn't follow the app. If you move Frame Job, copy the command again and register the new path.

The button isn't an edit, so no agent tool does the same thing.

### The missing helper warning

If the helper is missing from this copy of Frame Job, or can't be run, **Copy MCP Command** is dimmed and the status line reads "framejob-mcp is missing from this copy of Frame Job."

Frame Job checks each time Settings opens. If the helper disappears while the window is open, pressing the button copies nothing and shows the same line.

## Testing a second copy

This is for testing, not everyday use. Setting the environment variable `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` to a path moves the socket there, so a test copy of Frame Job stays apart from your everyday one. Set it for both Frame Job and `framejob-mcp`.

Setting it for the helper alone is often enough. When a tool call finds nothing at that path, the helper launches the copy it belongs to and passes the path on. See [A custom socket path](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#a-custom-socket-path) for the rules.

## Related

- [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/)
- [The helper and the socket](/mcp/helper-and-socket/)
- [A typical session](/mcp/typical-session/)
- [Settings](/reference/settings/)

A forwarded tool call can take as long as it needs, so a long recording or analysis is never cut off by the helper. Only the helper's own request for the tool list has a limit, the [5 seconds](/mcp/overview/#the-tool-list-with-frame-job-closed) before it falls back to the stored list.

A `ping` is answered even while a long call holds the app, because the helper answers it itself.

If the client closes, the helper exits at once, without waiting for a call in flight.

### Errors from the helper

A call the helper couldn't deliver comes back as an ordinary tool result with `isError: true` and a plain sentence, so a model can read it.

| The call answers | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `could not connect to Frame Job at <path>: <reason>` | The socket is there but can't be reached, for example because of its permissions. |
| `/usr/bin/open <bundle> failed (<status>): <reason>` | macOS couldn't launch the app. |
| `Frame Job did not answer at <socket> within …` | See [Failed launches](#failed-launches). |
| `could not read Frame Job's answer at <path>: the answer is over 8 MiB` | The helper won't read an answer larger than 8 MiB. |
| `HOME is not set, so the agent socket's path is unknown` | The helper started with no home folder in its environment, and no custom path. |

Other failures are JSON-RPC errors:

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `-32700` | The line isn't JSON. The answer has a null id. |
| `-32600` | The message is a batch, or isn't a JSON object. A batch and a non-object answer with a null id. A method that isn't a string answers this too, with the request's id. |
| `-32601` | Frame Job isn't answering and the method is one the helper can't handle itself, or Frame Job doesn't know the method. |
| `-32603` | The tool list couldn't be answered from the app or from the stored copy, `Contents/Resources/agent-catalog.json`. The message names both reasons. |

The helper passes any method but `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list` and `tools/call` to the app when it answers. Notifications and responses from a client are dropped and never forwarded.

The helper's standard output carries protocol only. Everything else it says goes to standard error, each line starting `framejob-mcp: `, so that's where to look in a client's logs.

### Protocol versions

Frame Job speaks three MCP protocol revisions: `2024-11-05`, `2025-03-26` and `2025-06-18`. It answers with the revision a client asks for, or `2025-06-18` if it asks for any other. The app and the helper work from the same list.

The helper's `initialize` answer names the server `framejob`, gives the version of the Frame Job it belongs to, and declares tools with `listChanged`.

### Tool list changes

A list from the stored copy can differ from the running app's, for example when another copy of Frame Job holds the socket. So after a client gets the stored list, or after a launch, the helper asks the app for its list following the next forwarded call. If it differs from what the client was last given, the helper sends `notifications/tools/list_changed` and the client can read it again.

The lists are compared by their content, so a difference in key order doesn't count.
